req.title: Reflect query parameters on GET
req.statement: The system shall include client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key of the GET /get response body.
expected_outcomes: response args field mirrors query string

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /get must reflect client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key. I designed tests covering: (1) a positive EP case with a single k=v pair asserting exact key and value; (2) a positive EP case with multiple parameters; (3) a negative path with no query parameters asserting args is an empty dict; (4) a BVA case with an empty-value parameter; (5) a BVA case with a parameter whose value contains special characters; (6) a DT case verifying that args does NOT bleed into other top-level keys; (7) a NEG case verifying that POST /post does not satisfy the GET /get contract. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant, operator, and key-name mutations.

tests.name: test_single_query_param_reflected_in_args
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args key mirrors query string
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_single_query_param_reflected_in_args():
    r = client.get('/get?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert 'args' in body
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}
    assert len(body['args']) == 1

test_single_query_param_reflected_in_args()

tests.name: test_args_key_present_alongside_other_top_level_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Verify top-level structure contains exactly url, args, headers, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args is under correct key; other keys from get_dict are present/absent per spec
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_args_key_present_alongside_other_top_level_keys():
    r = client.get('/get?x=42')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['args'] == {'x': '42'}
    assert 'url' in body
    assert 'headers' in body
    assert 'origin' in body
    assert 'form' not in body
    assert 'data' not in body
    assert 'files' not in body
    assert 'json' not in body

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_does_not_satisfy_get_args_contract
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
POST /post endpoint is registered separately from GET /get
actions: Confirm GET /get?foo=bar returns args with foo=bar
Confirm POST /post?foo=bar also returns args with foo=bar but is a different endpoint
expected: POST /post returns HTTP 200 with args == {'foo': 'bar'} (different handler)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: GET /get is the specific endpoint; wrong method returns 405
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_endpoint_does_not_satisfy_get_args_contract():
    r_get = client.get('/get?foo=bar')
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    assert r_get.get_json()['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}
    r_post_on_get = client.post('/get?foo=bar')
    assert r_post_on_get.status_code == 405
    r_post = client.post('/post?foo=bar')
    assert r_post.status_code == 200
    assert r_post.get_json()['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}

test_post_endpoint_does_not_satisfy_get_args_contract()

actions: Assert args['k'] is a list ['1', '2'] per semiflatten logic
expected: args['k'] == ['1', '2'] (semiflatten returns list for multi-value keys)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: boundary — duplicate keys; semiflatten in helpers.py returns list when len > 1

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_duplicate_query_param_key_returns_list_or_last_value():
    r = client.get('/get?k=1&k=2')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert 'args' in body
    assert 'k' in body['args']
    assert body['args']['k'] == ['1', '2']

tests.name: test_args_value_is_string_not_integer
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Assert args['count'] is the string '99', not integer 99
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: query param values are always strings; catches type-coercion mutations
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_args_value_is_string_not_integer():
    r = client.get('/get?count=99')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['args']['count'] == '99'
    assert body['args']['count'] != 99
    assert isinstance(body['args']['count'], str)
    assert body['args'] == {'count': '99'}

test_args_value_is_string_not_integer()
